newsitem.title: USA: United sees 15-20 pct of EPS in Q1.
newsitem.headline: United sees 15-20 pct of EPS in Q1.

text.p: United Illuminating Co said Thursday it expects to see 15 percent to 20 percent of its annual earnings accrue in the first quarter.
The company also said it is in a suitable financial position to maintain its current annual dividend level of $2.88 "well into the future."
The company said its expected accrual of earnings in the first quarter reflects the impact of weather-adjusted sales, leap year factors, nuclear outages and higher fossil fuel expenses.

Robert Fiscus, the company's president and chief financial officer, said the recent rate decision by the Connecticut Department of Public Control gave the company more certainty as to its future earnings and cash flow from the utility business.

"We have an excellent chance to earn our allowed 11.5 percent return on equity, which would generate annual earnings in the $3.30-$3.40 range, well above the dividend level of $2.88, and our cash flow per share in 1996 was 3.6 times the dividend level," Fiscus said.

The company's chairman and chief executive, Richard Grossi, said a recent draft bill by the state legislature regarding utility restructuring should not impinge on its ability to earn a "reasonable" return and allows for full recovery of investments made in the regulatory era.
